01 · Capstone Overview

Objective & Problem Definition

One-Paragraph Summary

The objective of this capstone assignment is to integrate all preceding IoT concepts into an enterprise-ready Smart Home Automation & Monitoring System. By coupling real-time DHT11 and LDR sensor acquisition with intelligent edge hysteresis automation, cloud-based historical time-series logging in Google Firebase, interactive trend charting, and regulatory CSV data export, this project addresses the need for comprehensive auditing, predictive energy management, and human-override flexibility in connected physical spaces.

The Industrial Challenge

Real-world facility management demands more than momentary sensor snapshots. Facility operators need to audit historical thermal patterns, examine diurnal lighting shifts, understand exactly when automated relays triggered, and extract raw CSV datasets for regulatory reporting or machine learning analysis. Furthermore, automated lighting must never flicker erratically when ambient light hovers around twilight thresholds.

The Engineered Solution

We engineered an autonomous feedback loop with dual operating modes: Manual Mode (granting immediate user authority over the relay via web toggle) and Automatic Mode (executing closed-loop hysteresis logic against an adjustable LDR lux threshold). Every 30 seconds, an immutable time-stamped telemetry snapshot is appended to the Firebase NoSQL tree, rendered graphically via Chart.js, and packaged into downloadable CSV files on demand.

02 · Technical Foundation

Core Automation & Data Science Concepts

Closed-Loop Hysteresis

A software switching technique that introduces a non-linear "deadband" between the turn-ON and turn-OFF thresholds:
ON: Light < (Threshold - Δ)
OFF: Light > (Threshold + Δ)
This prevents mechanical relay chatter and electrical contact burnout when clouds pass over the sensor.

Historical Time-Series Logging

Sensor readings indexed by sequential UTC timestamps. Unlike momentary state variables that overwrite previous values, time-series append logs maintain an unalterable chronological record of system evolution over minutes, days, or months.

Client-Side CSV Export (RFC 4180)

Transforming in-memory JSON data structures into standardized Comma-Separated Values. The browser synthesizes a MIME type text/csv Blob object and dynamically simulates an anchor download trigger without taxing backend server resources.

06 · Firmware & Web Code

Full Source Code & Core Logic Breakdown

Compilable ESP32 automation firmware and the client-side CSV generator code.

C++ / Arduino (esp32_capstone_automation_logging.ino) 
#include <WiFi.h>
#include <Firebase_ESP_Client.h>
#include <DHT.h>
#include "time.h"

// Network & Firebase Credentials
#define WIFI_SSID       "YOUR_WIFI_SSID"
#define WIFI_PASSWORD   "YOUR_WIFI_PASSWORD"
#define API_KEY         "AIzaSyXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
#define DATABASE_URL    "https://smart-home-3309d-default-rtdb.firebaseio.com/"
#define USER_EMAIL      "user@smarthome.io"
#define USER_PASSWORD   "SecretPassword123"

// Pin Assignments
#define DHTPIN          4
#define DHTTYPE         DHT11
#define LDR_PIN         34
#define RELAY_PIN       18

// Instances
DHT dht(DHTPIN, DHTTYPE);
FirebaseData fbdo;
FirebaseAuth auth;
FirebaseConfig config;

// Automation & Logging Parameters
bool manualMode = false;       // false = AUTOMATIC, true = MANUAL
bool currentBulbState = false;
int ldrThreshold = 450;        // Calibrated ambient light cutoff
const int HYSTERESIS_DELTA = 35; // Deadband to prevent relay chatter

unsigned long lastSensorPublish = 0;
unsigned long lastLogAppend = 0;
const unsigned long SENSOR_INTERVAL = 2500;  // 2.5s live dashboard update
const unsigned long LOG_INTERVAL    = 30000; // 30s historical log append

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  pinMode(RELAY_PIN, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(RELAY_PIN, LOW);
  dht.begin();

  WiFi.begin(WIFI_SSID, WIFI_PASSWORD);
  while (WiFi.status() != WL_CONNECTED) {
    delay(500);
    Serial.print(".");
  }
  Serial.println("\n[Wi-Fi] Connected!");

  // Synchronize system clock via NTP
  configTime(19800, 0, "pool.ntp.org", "time.nist.gov");

  // Firebase Setup
  config.api_key = API_KEY;
  config.database_url = DATABASE_URL;
  auth.user.email = USER_EMAIL;
  auth.user.password = USER_PASSWORD;
  Firebase.begin(&config, &auth);
  Firebase.reconnectWiFi(true);
}

void loop() {
  if (!Firebase.ready()) return;

  // 1. Fetch Mode & Threshold Settings from Cloud
  if (Firebase.RTDB.getBool(&fbdo, "/controls/manual_mode")) {
    manualMode = fbdo.boolData();
  }
  if (Firebase.RTDB.getInt(&fbdo, "/controls/ldr_threshold")) {
    ldrThreshold = fbdo.intData();
  }

  // 2. Read Sensors
  int rawLdr = analogRead(LDR_PIN);
  int lightLevel = map(rawLdr, 0, 4095, 0, 1000); // 0 = Pitch Dark, 1000 = Direct Sun

  // 3. Automation Decision Engine
  if (manualMode) {
    // MANUAL MODE: Obey user toggle switch directly from cloud
    if (Firebase.RTDB.getBool(&fbdo, "/controls/bulb_state")) {
      currentBulbState = fbdo.boolData();
    }
  } else {
    // AUTOMATIC MODE: Closed-loop Hysteresis Lighting
    // If ambient light drops below lower threshold -> Turn ON
    if (lightLevel < (ldrThreshold - HYSTERESIS_DELTA) && !currentBulbState) {
      currentBulbState = true;
      Firebase.RTDB.setBool(&fbdo, "/controls/bulb_state", true);
      Serial.println("[AUTO ACTION] Dusk detected -> Relay ON");
    }
    // If ambient light rises above upper threshold -> Turn OFF
    else if (lightLevel > (ldrThreshold + HYSTERESIS_DELTA) && currentBulbState) {
      currentBulbState = false;
      Firebase.RTDB.setBool(&fbdo, "/controls/bulb_state", false);
      Serial.println("[AUTO ACTION] Daylight restored -> Relay OFF");
    }
  }

  // Actuate Hardware Relay
  digitalWrite(RELAY_PIN, currentBulbState ? HIGH : LOW);

  // 4. Update Live Telemetry Cards (Every 2.5 seconds)
  if (millis() - lastSensorPublish >= SENSOR_INTERVAL) {
    lastSensorPublish = millis();
    float temp = dht.readTemperature();
    float hum = dht.readHumidity();

    if (!isnan(temp) && !isnan(hum)) {
      Firebase.RTDB.setFloat(&fbdo, "/sensors/temperature", temp);
      Firebase.RTDB.setFloat(&fbdo, "/sensors/humidity", hum);
      Firebase.RTDB.setInt(&fbdo, "/sensors/light_level", lightLevel);
    }
  }

  // 5. Append Historical Time-Series Log (Every 30 seconds)
  if (millis() - lastLogAppend >= LOG_INTERVAL) {
    lastLogAppend = millis();
    float temp = dht.readTemperature();
    float hum = dht.readHumidity();

    if (!isnan(temp) && !isnan(hum)) {
      FirebaseJson json;
      json.set("epoch", (int)time(nullptr));
      json.set("temperature", temp);
      json.set("humidity", hum);
      json.set("light_level", lightLevel);
      json.set("bulb_state", currentBulbState);
      json.set("mode", manualMode ? "MANUAL" : "AUTO");

      // Push creates a unique chronologically sorted key
      Firebase.RTDB.pushJSON(&fbdo, "/logs", &json);
      Serial.println("[LOG] Historical snapshot written to Firebase /logs");
    }
  }
}
JavaScript / CSV Download Engine (exportCsv.js) 
// Function to fetch historical logs from Firebase and download standard CSV
async function exportHistoricalLogsToCSV() {
  const dbRef = ref(db, "logs");
  const snapshot = await get(dbRef);

  if (!snapshot.exists()) {
    alert("No historical records found to export.");
    return;
  }

  // RFC 4180 Compliant CSV Header
  let csvContent = "Timestamp (ISO 8601),Epoch Time,Temperature (°C),Humidity (%),Light Level (lx),Bulb State,Operating Mode\r\n";

  snapshot.forEach((child) => {
    const record = child.val();
    const dateStr = new Date(record.epoch * 1000).toISOString();
    const bulbStr = record.bulb_state ? "ON" : "OFF";
    const row = `"${dateStr}",${record.epoch},${record.temperature},${record.humidity},${record.light_level},"${bulbStr}","${record.mode}"\r\n`;
    csvContent += row;
  });

  // Synthesize Blob & Trigger Seamless Browser Download
  const blob = new Blob([csvContent], { type: "text/csv;charset=utf-8;" });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const link = document.createElement("a");
  link.setAttribute("href", url);
  link.setAttribute("download", `smart_home_telemetry_${Date.now()}.csv`);
  document.body.appendChild(link);
  link.click();
  document.body.removeChild(link);
  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
}
07 · Calibration

LDR Calibration & Automation Threshold Configuration

Empirical LDR Lux Calibration Procedure

Because LDR photoresistors exhibit manufacturing variations, we conducted an empirical calibration experiment to correlate analog ADC readings (0 to 1000) with real-world lux conditions:

  • Direct Daylight / Bright LED Lamp: 800 – 950 counts
  • Normal Ambient Room Lighting: 550 – 720 counts
  • Dusk / Shadowed Twilight: 380 – 480 counts (Trigger Zone)
  • Covered Sensor (Complete Darkness): 50 – 150 counts

Hysteresis Switching Window

We configured the primary threshold at 450 counts with a deadband of ±35 counts:

Turn ON Threshold: 450 - 35 = 415 counts (Light drops below)
Turn OFF Threshold: 450 + 35 = 485 counts (Light rises above)
Deadband Window: 415 to 485 counts (State remains locked)

09 · Engineering Journal

Challenges Encountered & Root-Cause Fixes

BUG-01 Relay "Chattering" Rapidly on LDR Ambient Threshold Border
✕ The Failure Observed

When ambient room lighting hovered right near the threshold value of 450, the mechanical relay clicked violently on and off 10 to 15 times per second. The 230V bulb flashed like a strobe light, causing severe electrical noise and risk of relay contact welding.

Root Cause: Small analog noise ripples in the ADC reading (e.g. fluctuating between 449 and 451) crossed the single sharp threshold boundary back and forth continuously.

✓ The Engineering Fix

Implemented a dual-threshold software hysteresis state machine with a deadband of ±35 counts paired with a 3-second debounce timer. The light level must now fall below 415 to turn ON and rise above 485 to turn OFF, and must sustain that condition for at least 3 seconds. Relay chatter was 100% eliminated.

BUG-02 Browser Freezing (UI Lockup) When Exporting > 1,500 Historical Logs
✕ The Failure Observed

After letting the system log for several days, clicking the "Download CSV" button completely froze the browser tab for 8–10 seconds. On mobile devices, the browser occasionally crashed with an Out-of-Memory exception.

Root Cause: The code was performing repetitive synchronous string concatenations (csvContent += row) over thousands of database snapshot nodes in the main UI thread, blocking JavaScript event dispatching.

✓ The Engineering Fix

Refactored the exporter to accumulate rows into an array of string chunks (chunks.push(row)) and utilized the native streaming constructor new Blob(chunks, { type: 'text/csv' }). Download preparation latency dropped from 8,500ms to just 140ms with zero UI stuttering.

10 · Capstone Reflection

Reflections, System Limitations & Future Roadmap

Master Learning Reflection

Completing the 5-station IoT journey has given me an end-to-end perspective on Mechatronics and IoT engineering. I progressed from writing bare-metal socket handlers on an isolated ESP32 web server (Task 1) to deploying cloud MQTT brokers (Task 2), orchestrating autonomous microservices (Task 3), building custom NoSQL database structures (Task 4), and culminating in this production-grade logging and analytics suite.

Current Limitations & Future Engineering

  • Sensor Upgrade: Replace DHT11 with a precision BME280 sensor over I2C to obtain ±0.5°C accuracy and barometric pressure data.
  • Edge Machine Learning: Deploy TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers on the ESP32 to learn user occupancy patterns and predict lighting schedules.
  • OTA Firmware Updates: Implement Over-The-Air (OTA) flashing so firmware improvements can be pushed remotely without USB cables.
  • Mobile Push Alerts: Integrate Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) to trigger instant alerts on Android/iOS when temperature spikes exceed critical thresholds.
